description:
## Destination

A spec in `docs/specs/` plus an ADR for the core mechanism, sharp enough to hand to `/to-tickets`, for a turnkey-maintained tool that makes `tk test` reuse recorded results for unchanged tests.

## Notes

- Domain: buck2 test execution in turnkey and in consumer repos. The tool ships to consumers the way `tk` and `tw` do. Turnkey's own repo is the first user.
- **Test result caching** means what `CONTEXT.md` says: buck2 caches build actions but never re-uses test results, and that gap is what this effort closes.
- Constraints every ticket must respect:
  - **Local hits are required.** Re-running `tk test //...` with nothing changed uses recorded results. Hits must survive, in order: the same daemon, daemon restarts, `buck2 clean`, and other checkouts on the same machine (jj workspaces, git worktrees).
  - **Remote execution is the eventual way to share results across machines.** Whatever local mechanism is chosen, pointing it at a standard remote-execution endpoint must be enough, with no redesign.
  - **Platforms:** darwin and Linux both get local hits. Reusing results across platforms is not a goal.
  - **Languages:** Go, Rust and Python (upstream prelude rules), Solidity and Jsonnet (turnkey's own rules). TypeScript joins once `typescript_test` exists.
  - **quokka** (github.com/njaremko/quokka) is a reference only. We build our own tool in this repo.
  - Anything that mirrors buck2's test-runner protocol or another buck2 wire format is pinned to the **exact** buck2 version turnkey ships.
  - **A turnkey-owned buck2 prelude is on the table.** "Needs a prelude change" is a cost to weigh, never a reason to rule an option out. Turnkey already builds its own prelude (`nix/buck2/prelude.nix`: upstream + `nix/patches/prelude/` + `nix/buck2/prelude-extensions/`) and extends it for languages the upstream prelude lacks. Changing upstream rule behaviour, e.g. making Go/Python tests use project-relative paths, is fair game.
- Facts gathered while charting (2026-09-25):
  - Upstream buck2 has opt-in test execution caching: the rule's `supports_test_execution_caching` flag, used together with an executor that doesn't disable caching. It only hits for tests that a remote-execution worker ran. The source says "We never upload local test executions". There is no local disk action cache.
  - Build actions *can* upload locally produced results (`allow_cache_uploads`).
  - Turnkey pins buck2-2026-04-15. No remote execution or cache is configured, and CI runs no tests.
- Skills: `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling` for grilling tickets, `/research` for research tickets, `/prototype` for prototypes. Use `CONTEXT.md` vocabulary.
- Research findings land in `docs/research/<name>.md` on `main`. Research agents work in a throwaway jj workspace, and the commit is folded into `main`. The research ticket gets a permalink to the file.
- When no tickets remain, compile Decisions so far into the spec, with the mechanism ADR under `docs/adr/`.

## Decisions so far

<!-- the index — one line per closed ticket: enough to judge relevance, then zoom the link for the detail the ticket holds -->
- [What test-caching support does our pinned buck2 have?](turnkey-w55.1) — pinned buck2 (7600cb80) serves test hits only from an RE action cache, and only for tests an RE worker ran; local test runs are never uploaded, but local *build* actions can be (`allow_cache_uploads`); no sqlite local cache; patching buck2 means building it from source.
- [What do turnkey's test targets read beyond their declared inputs?](turnkey-w55.3) — go_test/python_test embed absolute checkout paths (no cross-checkout reuse without a prelude change); worst wrong-hit risks are solidity_test (forge picks solc from $HOME, unseeded fuzzing, soldeps sources unkeyed) and python3-via-PATH; test env is scrubbed to six vars; caching is only sound under `tk` (stale-cell detection).
- [Which remote-execution-API servers can run on a developer machine?](turnkey-w55.2) — cache-only: bazel-remote fits (nixpkgs, single binary, LRU, hit validation, proxies to a shared backend); darwin-native local workers exist only in NativeLink (FSL licence, not in nixpkgs) and Buildbarn (multi-process, platform-property mismatch with buck2); nothing sandboxes on darwin; keys are buck2-computed, so backends are swappable.
- [How does Bazel decide when a test result is reusable?](turnkey-w55.4) — key = everything the test process sees (incl. inherited env values, timeout, filters, platform); policy (auto/yes/no, `external`) sits outside the key; only passes are shared and cached failures are misses; flakiness not keyed; hits shown as `(cached)` with original logs; hermeticity assumed, not checked.
- [When may a recorded test result be reused?](turnkey-w55.5) — only passes are reused; on by default with one `no-test-cache` label; `tk --no-test-cache test` skips reads but still records; key = everything the process sees + buck2/tool version salt; a wrong hit is never acceptable (when in doubt, miss); only under `tk`; policy stays outside the key.

## Not yet specified

- **Prototype.** Try the leading mechanism, or two, on a real turnkey test target once the mechanism candidates narrow.
- **buck2 version.** Does the chosen mechanism need a buck2 bump (e.g. for `sqlite_dep_file_state`) or a carried buck2 patch?
- **Shared-cache handover.** Who may write to a shared cache (CI only, or everyone)? What is the trust model? May results from local runs be uploaded? Whether a publish-only opt-out label is needed (deferred from the reuse policy, which has only `no-test-cache`).
- **Implementation language** of the tool (Rust or Go).
- **Cache lifecycle.** Where the local store lives, eviction and GC, and starting/stopping any local service.

## Out of scope

- Choosing or deploying a shared remote-execution backend. The spec assumes a standard endpoint.
- Re-enabling tests in CI (separate effort).
- Writing `typescript_test`. The spec only says how TS gets caching once that rule exists.
- Caching or batching per individual test case. v1 caches whole test targets.
- Target determination and flaky-test management (see `CONTEXT.md`).
title: Test result caching for turnkey's buck2 tests
